explanation: A central figure in Judaism, Christianity and Islam, who according to Exodus was born of a Hebrew woman and saved from death by Pharaoh's daughter.
The longest river in Africa and an important symbol in Egyptian culture and religion; Moses was found in a basket along the banks of the Nile.
An ancient Semitic people who were the ancestors of Israel and lived as slaves in Egypt under Pharaoh's rule.
Moses' sister, who helped save him from death and later became a prophetess and leader of the women of Israel.
The woman who rescued Moses from the Nile and adopted him as her own son, even though she knew he was a Hebrew.
A region in the northwestern part of the Arabian Peninsula where Moses fled after killing an Egyptian and married Jethro's daughter, Zipporah.
A Midianite priest and Moses' father-in-law, who gave advice and support to Moses during his leadership of the people of Israel.
A miraculous phenomenon in which God spoke to Moses through a bush that burned without being consumed; this was the beginning of Moses' calling as God's servant and leader of the people of Israel.
